D010-D006_h001.question:
I’ve kind of been all over the place this past year. About… two months back, it was like someone flipped a switch. I barely slept and didn’t feel tired, just buzzing all day. I’d finish my delivery shift and still want to keep driving around, planning “big moves.” I started talking nonstop—customers, coworkers, anyone—I’d get irritated if people tried to cut me off or if things got quiet. My mood would jump from feeling on top of the world to snapping at someone over nothing.

Around that time, I got really fixated on sex—hookup apps, risky stuff I normally wouldn’t do. I even put a bunch of money, like most of my savings, into this sketchy delivery “startup idea” with some guy I barely know, without really reading anything.

I’ve also had moments where I’m sure this girl I’ve been seeing is cheating on me, even though I don’t really have proof. Sometimes I see people in my apartment or on the street—just standing there or moving past me—and then they’re gone when I look twice.

Before all that, and again more recently, I’ve had months where I just feel low, empty. Things I used to enjoy—music on the road, hanging out—don’t feel like anything. Even picking what to eat or what route to take feels overwhelming. It’s been about five months total like that, and it’s gotten hard to keep up with work and basic stuff.
D010-D006_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h001.answer: A & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h002.question:
It’s been a really strange year. About eight months ago I went through this…high, I guess, that lasted a couple of months. I was constantly on edge and snappy, like the smallest thing my husband said would set me off. At the same time, I had so much energy I could barely sit through a Zoom meeting. I’d pace between my desk and the kitchen, start three analyses at once, then jump to planning collaborations with people I barely knew.

I was talking nonstop, in lab Slack, in meetings, even texting old classmates at 2 a.m. I felt weirdly bold socially, reaching out to senior PIs on Twitter like we were old friends. I even put a big chunk of our savings into this startup doing “AI for genomics” after only skimming their website; my husband was furious, and honestly I don’t know what I was thinking.

Around that time I became convinced something was wrong inside my body—like my organs were decaying, even though all my tests were normal. I’d also get these strange, metallic or chemical tastes out of nowhere, like I’d swallowed lab reagents.

After that, I crashed. For the last five months I’ve felt really low and flat, mostly staying in our apartment, avoiding friends and even family calls. Work has been a mess; I stare at code and can’t keep a clear line of thought, like my brain is under water. Even answering simple emails feels overwhelming. My husband says I’m not myself at all.
D010-D006_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h002.answer: A & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h003.question:

D010-D006_h004.question:

D010-D006_h005.question:

I just felt incredibly good, almost high for no reason.

Around then and since, I’ve had this recurring sense that comments on TV or random posts online are somehow directed at me, like there’s a hidden message about our company or my decisions. Sometimes I get this odd metallic or bitter taste in my mouth when there’s nothing there, like I’ve eaten something spoiled.

The last five months have been the opposite: I feel flat and hollow, like everything is meaningless. I’ve lost interest in golf, in reading business journals—stuff I used to enjoy. I’m falling behind at work because I can’t concentrate; I keep misplacing documents and forgetting conversations, and it scares me. It’s like I’m here, but not really in my own life anymore.

D010-D006_h006.question:

I’ll pace the apartment, then decide at 2 a.m. to drive out to the coast at 120 km/h “to chase a shot,” even though there’s no actual project. I’ve blown a lot of money on gear I don’t need, and I’ve driven after barely sleeping, telling myself I react faster than other people anyway.

My temper’s gotten weird. The smallest thing—an assistant asking a basic question, my ex texting about our son—sets me off. I snap, bark at people on set, then five minutes later I’m talking nonstop, jumping from one idea to the next. It feels physically uncomfortable to be quiet, like if I stop talking, I’ll lose something important.

I keep feeling like I’m on the verge of a breakthrough film that will “change the conversation” globally, like I’m uniquely chosen to tell certain stories. Sometimes, when I’m lying in bed trying to wind down, I feel a crawling or buzzing on my skin, like invisible insects or fingers brushing my arms, but there’s nothing there when I look. It’s all starting to mess with work and with seeing my kid.

A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h007.question:

I’ll wake up feeling on top of the world, almost buzzing, talking a mile a minute, planning new projects for my class, texting friends nonstop, and then suddenly I’m snapping at people for no real reason. Another thing that’s freaking me out is I keep thinking something terrible is about to happen to everyone, like the world is just going to end or collapse somehow. It feels so real it’s hard to argue with. Sometimes when I’m lying in bed or sitting at my desk, I feel like something is crawling on my skin or brushing past me, but there’s nothing there. It’s making it hard to teach, to sleep, to trust my own head.

D010-D006_h020.question:
I’ve been feeling really off for a long time now. For about seven months I’ve just been…low. I drag myself to my shifts, but I don’t care about anything the way I used to. I used to go out with my coworkers after nights, do yoga, that sort of thing. Now I just go straight home and lie there. I feel sad pretty much all day, most days. It’s hard to enjoy even simple things like watching a show.

I can’t fall asleep easily; I just lie in bed for hours, going over everything I’ve done wrong. I think a lot about not wanting to be here anymore—not with a plan, but more like wishing I wouldn’t wake up.

A few months ago there was this three‑week period where I swung the other way. I was on edge and snapping at everyone—patients, doctors, even my mom. I couldn’t sit still, was pacing the unit, talking nonstop at work so fast people told me to slow down. Around that time I started to feel like something was seriously wrong inside my body, like my organs were rotting or malfunctioning, even though tests were normal. Sometimes I hear this voice, kind of outside my own thoughts, telling me there’s something wrong with me or that I’m a burden. I still hear it on and off.

    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D010-D006_h021.question:
It’s been a rough few months. First it was this low stretch that’s been going on maybe two months now. I just stopped caring about pretty much everything, even stuff I used to be proud of. At the factory, I move like I’m underwater. The guys on my line complain I’m too slow picking parts up, and I can feel my body just not wanting to move faster. When I’m walking home after night shift, it’s like my legs are full of sand. In that time I’ve thought a lot about just ending it, down to where I’d do it and how, picturing it pretty clearly. That scares me, but it also feels…weirdly calm.

Before this low part, there was about two weeks where I was the complete opposite. I was snapping at everyone over nothing, like any small thing set me off. I had so much energy I couldn’t sit still, pacing through the break room, starting three jobs at once and finishing none because my mind kept jumping around.

On and off through all of this, I get these ideas that my ex is sneaking around with someone else, even though we’re not really together and I don’t have proof. I check his socials, drive past his place after work. Sometimes at night, on the walk home, I see people standing by the road, or a shadow moving that looks like a person—but when I get closer, there’s no one there. I can’t always tell if it’s just me being tired from night shifts or something else, but it feels very real in the moment.

    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h022.question:
I guess this started around three months ago. For about two weeks I was just…amped. I was barely sleeping but didn’t feel tired. I’d sit at my desk to audit code and five minutes later I’d be jumping to another project, another window, another idea. I couldn’t stick with anything. Little things set me off—someone questioning my report, a Slack message worded the wrong way—and I’d snap, get really angry, which isn’t usually me.

At the same time I got this fixed idea that I was on some different level from other people in infosec, like I could see patterns in networks that no one else could, and that maybe some government agencies were quietly watching me because of how “unique” my skills were. Sometimes when I was up late at my rig, I’d feel this crawling or buzzing on my arms or the back of my neck, like something was brushing against my skin, but there’d be nothing there.

Then it all crashed. For the last two months I’ve been moving in slow motion—walking slower, even reaching for a coffee mug feels like effort. I stare at my terminal and just can’t bring myself to type. I’ve missed deadlines, stopped answering friends. I don’t really care if I lose my job. A few weeks ago I collected all my leftover meds and some painkillers, thinking I’d just end it. I didn’t go through with it, but I hid the pills in my room and wrote a kind of goodbye note on my laptop.
D010-D006_h022.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D010-D006_h023.question:
Well, over this past year I’ve been on this sort of rollercoaster. About three months ago I had this spell that lasted maybe two weeks where I just felt…too good. Not normal good. I was buzzing. I hardly slept, but I wasn’t tired. I’d be pacing around the house at 3 a.m., starting one thing, then dropping it and jumping to another. I couldn’t sit through a whole TV show or even finish a cup of tea without getting up. My kids said I was talking too fast, spending too much, calling old colleagues with “big plans.” I honestly felt like I could do anything.

Around that same time, I became convinced that an old doctor I worked with is secretly in love with me. I know it sounds silly at my age, but I can’t shake the feeling; sometimes I even hear his voice, as clear as if he were in the room, telling me I’m special or that we’re meant to be. Other times the voices just murmur my name.

Lately it’s been the opposite. For about two months now I’ve been moving like I’m underwater. Getting dressed feels like a full shift on the ward. I just sit in my chair staring at the garden, no drive to cook, to see friends, anything. Even walking to the mailbox is slow and heavy. I keep thinking, “What’s the point? Maybe it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up.” I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but those thoughts show up every day. It’s gotten hard to manage my bills and medications, and I’ve let a lot of things slide.
D010-D006_h023.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D010-D006_h023.answer: B & A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h024.question:
I’m not really sure where to start. Over the last few months I just haven’t felt like myself at all. I’m a nurse on nights, and it’s gotten to the point where I’m barely functioning at work.

There was this stretch, maybe a couple of weeks, where I was all over the place. I’d come into a shift buzzing, talking fast, feeling like I could handle everything at once, then suddenly snap at people over nothing. I couldn’t sit still on breaks; I’d be pacing the hallway, reorganizing supplies, starting three different chart notes and not finishing any of them. At home I’d jump from cleaning the kitchen, to planning some big project, to scrolling job postings, and nothing actually got done.

Lately it’s swung the other way. For the past couple of months I’ve lost interest in pretty much everything I used to enjoy—yoga, seeing friends, even watching shows. I still can’t sit still though; I pace my apartment, pick at my skin, wring my hands. Sometimes, walking over the hospital bridge or standing at a busy street, I get this intense urge to just jump or step out, which scares me.

On top of that, I keep feeling like people are watching me—coworkers, maybe even the hospital administration—like they’re tracking what I do. Sometimes I hear my name being called or a voice commenting on what I’m doing when no one’s actually there. I can’t tell if I’m just exhausted or if something is really wrong.

    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D010-D006_h025.question:
I work as a sound engineer, so I’m used to long, weird hours, but about two months ago things got…off. For two weeks I felt insanely good, like I was plugged into a power outlet. I barely slept and didn’t feel tired. I’d wake up buzzing with ideas—remixing old tracks, redesigning my whole studio, starting a podcast—all at the same time. I’d start wiring new gear, then jump to editing an entire album, then sketch out some giant live-show concept, but nothing actually got finished. My boss said I was “all over the place” and clients stopped calling because I was missing deadlines.

Around that time, I started feeling like random stuff—radio ads, people’s conversations at the café—were kind of about me, like they were dropping hints or commenting on what I was doing. Sometimes I get weird tastes in my mouth out of nowhere, like metal or chemicals, even when I’m not eating anything.

After that high period crashed, I’ve spent the last couple of months moving in slow motion. Even walking to the train feels like wading through mud. I don’t really care about projects I used to be proud of; finishing a mix means nothing. I just think it’d be easier if I didn’t wake up sometimes—not that I’m planning anything, just…if I didn’t exist, it’d be a relief. It’s gotten hard to keep up with work and basic stuff like groceries and laundry.
